transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve been having these nights, usually after work or after a tense dinner, where I start eating and it kind of feels like something in me switches off. I know I’m reaching for more food, but I can’t really make myself stop.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever try to compensate for it by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or doing a lot of exercise?

Yeah… sometimes. Not every time, but there have been nights after everyone’s asleep where I go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. Sometimes I’ve taken laxatives too. I tell myself it’s just to… undo it, I guess. Then afterward I feel pretty ashamed and kind of shaky.

latest_inference.note: This turn ruled out F50.0 - Anorexia nervosa due to reported binge eating and compensatory behaviors rather than restrictive eating or fear of weight gain primarily. F50.9 - Eating disorder, unspecified and F32.9 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified were ruled out due to more specific eating disorder symptoms described. F43.00 - Acute stress reaction, unspecified is also ruled out as the symptoms are more aligned with an eating disorder.
